title: Art and Creativity

parts.title: Notices and messages
parts.instructions: For each notice, choose what it means.
notices: CITY ART GALLERY: Free entry on the first Sunday of every month. The new photography room is closed until 3 p.m. for cleaning. Tours of the main hall start at 11 a.m.
PAINTING CLASS: Please bring your own brushes. Paper and paints are provided. If you cannot come, tell Mrs Okoro at least one day before.
LOLA: I'm stuck in traffic! Can you go in and get the tickets for the exhibition? My card is the green one. I'll find you by the sculpture.

parts.title: A wall of fish
parts.instructions: Read the article and choose the best answer for each question.
parts.passage:
When the town council asked for volunteers to paint a mural on the wall of the old bus station, I was the first to put up my hand. I had never painted anything bigger than a postcard, but I love drawing, and I imagined a huge picture of the sea, with colourful fish swimming across it. My friends laughed and said that I was too ambitious.

We began in June, on a warm Saturday morning. There were eight of us, and a professional artist, a woman called Ms Dorsey, who told us what to do. The first thing she did was to give us a very large piece of paper and ask us to draw our ideas. Then we had to agree on one design. This was harder than I expected, because everybody had a different opinion. Eventually, we decided to paint the whole sea life of our local river.

The painting took five weekends. We stood on ladders, and our arms ached. A few times I dropped paint on my shoes, and once on Ms Dorsey. She just laughed. Strangers stopped to watch, and some of them brought us cold drinks, which we gladly accepted.

On the day it was finished, the mayor came to see it, and there was a small party. I looked at the wall and felt proud. Every time I walk past it now, I see a bit that I painted myself: a small, slightly crooked orange fish near the corner. Nobody else knows which one it is, and that is my secret.

questions.prompt: Why did the writer volunteer for the mural?
options: Her friends asked her to join.
She had won a prize for painting.
She wanted to paint something big and colourful.
The council paid her to paint.
questions.explanation: She loved drawing and imagined a huge picture of the sea with colourful fish.

questions.prompt: What was difficult about the planning?
options: Finding enough paint for the wall
questions.explanation: It was hard because everybody had a different opinion about the design.

questions.prompt: How did Ms Dorsey react when the writer dropped paint on her?
options: She was angry for a moment.
She asked her to be more careful.
questions.explanation: She just laughed.

questions.prompt: What did strangers do while the group was working?
options: They took photographs of the wall.
They offered to paint with them.
questions.explanation: Some strangers brought them cold drinks, which they accepted.

questions.prompt: What is the writer's secret?
questions.explanation: She says nobody else knows which small orange fish she painted.

parts.title: The artist of small stones
parts.instructions: Choose the sentence that fits each gap. There are three extra sentences.
parts.passage:
Pablo is twenty-four, and he is probably the only artist in his town who paints on pebbles. [1] Some of his pieces are no bigger than a coin, but when you look at them closely, you can see hundreds of tiny details.

He started during a walk on the beach when he was eight. His grandfather picked up a smooth stone and asked him to draw a face on it. [2] Years later, he still keeps that pebble on his desk.

Every few weeks, Pablo goes to the sea to collect new stones. He chooses them carefully, because the shape of each one gives him an idea. [3] A long, thin stone, for example, can become a bird or a fish.

His work is now sold in shops in six countries. [4] However, he never paints the same thing twice, and he refuses to make copies for factories.

Pablo also teaches children to paint pebbles at the local library. [5] "When they give one to their parents, you should see their faces," he says with a smile.
sentences: That simple game changed his life.
Some of the pebbles he paints are millions of years old.
A round one might look like an apple, a face or the moon.
Painting is not his main job, as he works in a bank.
People who see his stones often say they cannot believe that they were painted by hand.
He has never been to art school or taken a lesson.
The classes are free, and there is always a long waiting list.
Many people want to buy a piece because it is so unusual.

gaps.explanation: "The only artist who paints on pebbles" is followed by what people say about his work; the next sentence describes the size of the pieces.
His grandfather asked him to draw a face on a stone; "That simple game changed his life" leads to the pebble he still keeps.
The shape of each stone gives him an idea; "A round one might look like..." continues, and the next sentence gives another example.
His work is sold in six countries; "Many people want to buy a piece" explains why, and "However" introduces his rule about copies.
He teaches children at the library; the classes are free with a waiting list, and the next sentence is about the children's pride.

parts.title: Why do people make art?
parts.instructions: Choose the correct word for each gap.
parts.passage: People have made art since the beginning of history. The oldest paintings, which were found in caves, [1] from more than forty thousand years ago. Nobody knows exactly why early people painted, but some experts think that they wanted to tell stories about their lives. Today, we use art for many different [2]. Some people paint because it helps them to relax after a difficult day. Others use it to [3] their feelings, which can be hard to explain in words. Many hospitals now have art classes for patients, as doctors have noticed that painting can help people to [4] better. You do not have to be a great artist to enjoy it. The most important thing is to [5] yourself and not to worry about what other people [6] of your work.

questions.prompt: Gap 1
questions.explanation: "Come from" shows the time when the paintings were made.

questions.prompt: Gap 2
questions.explanation: "Different reasons" explains why people make art.

questions.prompt: Gap 3
questions.explanation: People "show" their feelings through art.

questions.prompt: Gap 4
questions.explanation: Doctors say painting helps people to feel better.

questions.prompt: Gap 5
questions.explanation: "Enjoy yourself" is the aim; the other verbs do not fit.

questions.prompt: Gap 6
questions.explanation: "What other people think of your work" is the correct expression.

parts.title: A letter about an art class
parts.instructions: Write one word in each gap.
parts.passage:
Dear Ines,
I have just joined an art class on Saturday mornings, and I love it! Our teacher is very patient, [1] she shows us how to mix colours. Last week, we painted a bowl of fruit, and mine looked [2] a pile of rocks. Everybody laughed, [3] me! I did not mind, because I know that I will get better [4] time. If you want to come [5] me next week, I can ask the teacher. The class costs £8, and you [6] not have to bring anything.
See you soon,
Beth

gaps.explanation: "And" joins two facts about the teacher: patient and shows how to mix colours.
"Looked like" compares her painting with a pile of rocks.
"Even me" adds a surprising person to the group that laughed.
"Come with me" is the correct expression.
The negative form "do not have to" needs the auxiliary do.

parts.title: Short conversations
parts.instructions: Listen to seven short conversations. Choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: aldwin
turns.text: Attention, visitors. Thank you for coming to the Riverside Gallery today. We normally close at six, as it says at the entrance, but today is different because the staff need to prepare a new exhibition. So the gallery will close at five o’clock, one hour before usual. The doors for the opening party at seven are for invited guests only, so if you do not have an invitation, please leave in good time. The shop and the café will also close early. You still have time to see the sculpture room on the first floor, which is the most popular one. Thank you for your understanding.

question.prompt: When does the gallery close today?
question.explanation: The usual closing time is six and the party at seven is for guests only, but today the gallery closes one hour earlier, at five.

turns.speaker: dashwood
turns.text: Are you ready for your first pottery class tomorrow, Cosima?

turns.speaker: cosima
turns.text: Nearly. I wasn’t sure what to take. Do I need boots? The studio floor might be wet.

turns.speaker: dashwood
turns.text: Not at all. It’s inside, and there’s a clean floor. I think the teacher said you don’t need anything special for your feet.

turns.speaker: cosima
turns.text: Good. And a notebook? I thought about taking notes.

turns.speaker: dashwood
turns.text: I did that in my first class, but you can’t hold a pen with muddy hands. Just watch and listen.

turns.speaker: cosima
turns.text: Fair. What about my clothes? Clay gets everywhere.

turns.speaker: dashwood
turns.text: Take Mum’s old cooking apron, the blue one in the kitchen drawer. It saved my jumper last year.

turns.speaker: cosima
turns.text: Brilliant idea!

question.prompt: What should the girl take to the pottery class?
question.explanation: The floor is clean so she does not need boots, and notes are useless with muddy hands; she needs something for her clothes, Mum’s old apron.

turns.speaker: elspeth
turns.text: Good morning. Can I help you?

turns.speaker: fitzroy
turns.text: Two tickets for the exhibition, please. One for me and one for my son.

turns.speaker: elspeth
turns.text: Certainly. Adults pay eight pounds. How old is your son?

turns.speaker: fitzroy
turns.text: He’s ten.

turns.speaker: elspeth
turns.text: Then he pays four pounds, because children under twelve get half price.

turns.speaker: fitzroy
turns.text: Is there a cheaper ticket? I read about a family offer.

turns.speaker: elspeth
turns.text: That’s only on Sundays, I’m afraid. Today is Saturday.

turns.speaker: fitzroy
turns.text: Oh well. I’ll pay by card. Do you need my son’s name?

turns.speaker: elspeth
turns.text: No, that’s fine. Here are your tickets. Enjoy the exhibition.

question.prompt: How much will the man pay in total?
question.explanation: The father pays eight pounds and his ten-year-old son pays four, and the family offer is only on Sundays, so the total is twelve pounds.

turns.speaker: godfrey
turns.text: Welcome to the Mill Museum. Many visitors ask where they can leave their coats, so let me explain. At the main entrance there used to be a rack, but it was removed last year, because people sometimes took the wrong coat. In the café you can hang your coat on your chair, but we cannot look after it there. So the best place is the cloakroom. It is downstairs, on the left side of the big hall, and it is free. The staff there will also look after bags and umbrellas, but please keep your money and phone with you. Enjoy your visit!

question.prompt: Where can visitors leave their coats?
question.explanation: The rack at the entrance was removed and the café is not safe, so the cloakroom downstairs is the place.

turns.speaker: imelda
turns.text: Jerome, I got your message. Is the drawing class still on Tuesday?

turns.speaker: jerome
turns.text: That was the old day. They moved it because the teacher has another job on Tuesdays.

turns.speaker: imelda
turns.text: To Wednesday? I saw that on the website.

turns.speaker: jerome
turns.text: That’s the photography class. I was confused too, so I checked the email twice. The drawing class is a day later than that one.

turns.speaker: imelda
turns.text: Oh, good. Thursday is better for me anyway. I work late on the other days.

turns.speaker: jerome
turns.text: Mine too. And the class will be in the same room, so nothing else changes.

turns.speaker: imelda
turns.text: Perfect. I’ll bring my new pencils.

question.prompt: Which day is the drawing class now?
question.explanation: Tuesday is the old day and Wednesday is the photography class; drawing is one day later than that, so it is Thursday.

turns.speaker: kingsley
turns.text: Hello everyone, my name’s Kingsley and I’m going to tell you about my paintings. When I started, I only used blue, because I love the sea and I painted boats all the time. My teacher said it was a bit boring, so I tried green last year for forests and fields. I used lots of it, and my mum put one of those pictures on the fridge. But my favourite colour now is a different one. I put it everywhere: in the sun, on the flowers, even on the faces, and my friends say my pictures look happy because of it. I buy a new tube every week because it finishes so fast. Thank you for listening.

question.prompt: Which colour does Kingsley use most now?
question.explanation: He used blue and then green in the past, but now he uses the colour of the sun and the flowers, which is yellow.

turns.speaker: merrick
turns.text: That’s a lovely painting above your sofa, Nanette. Is it by a famous artist?

turns.speaker: nanette
turns.text: People always ask that! It looks professional, but no.

turns.speaker: merrick
turns.text: Did your sister paint it? I know she studies art.

turns.speaker: nanette
turns.text: She does, but she paints modern things with lots of colours. This one is a quiet scene of a farm, and the paint is very old. My grandmother painted it when she was young, before she got married.

turns.speaker: merrick
turns.text: She was very talented.

turns.speaker: nanette
turns.text: She never thought so. She gave it to me when I moved into this flat, and I’ll never sell it.

question.explanation: It looks professional but it is not by a famous artist, and her sister paints modern things; her grandmother painted the old farm.

parts.title: Understanding the main idea
parts.instructions: Listen to six short conversations and choose the best answer.

turns.speaker: ottoline3
turns.text: Have you thought about our art project? Maybe we could copy a famous painting, like the sunflowers.

turns.speaker: pembroke
turns.text: Mr Dunn hates copies. He wants something original. What about a portrait of him? He’d love it.

turns.speaker: ottoline3
turns.text: He would hate that even more! He’s very shy. I think we should paint something we see every day. Like the view from the school bridge, with the river and the old mill.

turns.speaker: pembroke
turns.text: That’s not a bad idea. And it’s easy to see it, we cross every day.

turns.speaker: ottoline3
turns.text: Exactly, and the light there in the evening is beautiful.

turns.speaker: pembroke
turns.text: OK, let’s go on Friday with our sketchbooks.

question.prompt: What do the friends decide to paint?
options: A copy of a famous picture
A view of their own town
question.explanation: The teacher does not like copies and is too shy for a portrait, so they agree on the view from the school bridge.

turns.speaker: radcliffe
turns.text: What are you going to get your aunt for her birthday?

turns.speaker: quenby
turns.text: I thought about painting a picture of her garden. But it would take weeks, and I’m not good enough.

turns.speaker: radcliffe
turns.text: Then try this shop. I saw some nice things there.

turns.speaker: quenby
turns.text: I looked there yesterday, but I only found ugly mugs. Still, they have scarves in lots of colours.

turns.speaker: radcliffe
turns.text: Shall we look in the market, then?

turns.speaker: quenby
turns.text: No, I’m tired, and I don’t want to spend all day shopping. She’s always cold, so I’ll get the blue one. It’s silk and it was in the window.

turns.speaker: radcliffe
turns.text: Perfect. She’ll love it.

question.prompt: What does the woman decide to do?
options: Buy a scarf as a gift
Paint a picture for her aunt
question.explanation: A painting would take weeks and she does not want to search more; she chooses the silk scarf that her aunt will like.

turns.speaker: thisbe
turns.text: Excuse me, may I speak to you? I’m a bit annoyed.

turns.speaker: sinclair
turns.text: Of course. What happened?

turns.speaker: thisbe
turns.text: Well, it’s not the noise, the school group is very quiet, and it’s not the temperature either, which is perfectly fine. It’s the people near the statue in room three. Three of them touched it just now, and one even leaned on it.

turns.speaker: sinclair
turns.text: Oh dear. There’s a sign.

turns.speaker: thisbe
turns.text: I know, but nobody reads it. Could you speak to them?

turns.speaker: sinclair
turns.text: Right away. Thank you for telling me.

question.explanation: She says that the noise and the temperature are fine, but several visitors touched the statue and one leaned on it.

turns.speaker: upton
turns.text: You look happy today, Verena. Are you going away for the summer?

turns.speaker: verena_x
turns.text: No, we’re staying here this year. But guess what! I found out last night that my sister is going to be in the new exhibition at the town hall.

turns.speaker: upton
turns.text: Did she win the school competition, then?

turns.speaker: verena_x
turns.text: She entered it last year but didn’t win. This time she didn’t enter anything. The organisers asked her, because they saw her photos online. She’s so nervous, but I’m really proud and excited.

turns.speaker: upton
turns.text: That’s brilliant news. Can we go to see it?

turns.speaker: verena_x
turns.text: Of course, it opens on the tenth. I’ll take you.

options: Her sister's work will be shown.
question.explanation: There is no holiday and no prize this time; the organisers asked her sister to show her photos.

turns.speaker: xenia
turns.text: Did you like the modern painting? It’s only three black lines on a white wall.

turns.speaker: winthrop_x
turns.text: I did, strangely. Some people say it’s too simple, or it’s a waste of time. But I stood there for ten minutes.

turns.speaker: xenia
turns.text: Why? What did you see?

turns.speaker: winthrop_x
turns.text: Nothing, really, but I felt calm and a bit sad. I think that’s the point. Art doesn’t have to be easy to understand or pretty. It’s good when it moves you.

turns.speaker: xenia
turns.text: I’d never thought like that. For me it’s about skill.

turns.speaker: winthrop_x
turns.text: That’s fair, but I like the feeling more.

question.prompt: What does the boy think good art should do?
question.explanation: He does not mind that it is simple or hard to understand; he stood there for ten minutes and says that art is good when it moves you.

turns.speaker: yardley
turns.text: Zenobia, you look terrible. What’s wrong?

turns.speaker: zenobia
turns.text: I think I lost my bag on the bus. My bus pass was inside, and my drawings for the art class.

turns.speaker: yardley
turns.text: Oh no! Well, you can get another bus pass, and you can draw again. Is that all?

turns.speaker: zenobia
turns.text: No, my phone too. It had all of my photos, and my mum’s number. I can’t call anyone.

turns.speaker: yardley
turns.text: Use mine and call the bus company.

turns.speaker: zenobia
turns.text: Thanks. I don’t care about the drawings or the pass. I just want my phone back. It’s like losing my memory.

turns.speaker: yardley
turns.text: Let’s go to the office together.

question.prompt: What is the girl most upset about losing?
question.explanation: She says that she does not care about the drawings or the pass; she wants her phone back because of the photos and the number.

parts.title: A teacher talks about an art workshop
parts.instructions: Listen to the talk and complete each note. Write one or two words, a number, a date or a time.

turns.speaker: speaker-1
turns.text: Good evening, everyone, and welcome to the first lesson of our painting workshop. I’m Philomela, and I’ll be your teacher for the next eight weeks. We advertised a six-week course at first, but so many of you wanted more time that we made it longer. Let me tell you how things work. We meet every Wednesday evening, from half past six until nine. Some of you asked about Thursday, but that day is for the pottery group, and the art room can’t be used by two groups. The art room is on the second floor, at the end of the corridor. Please don’t go to the first floor, which has the music rooms, and don’t use the lift, it’s often broken. Painting is messy, so I need to tell you what to bring. You don’t have to bring brushes or paper, the school will give you those. But please bring an old shirt, because paint never comes off clothes. An apron isn’t enough, in my experience. Next, let me tell you about the plan. In the first three weeks we practise colours and shapes. In week four we are going to visit the museum on King Street, to see paintings by local artists. We’ll walk there together, because it’s only ten minutes. The old programme says we go to the gallery, but that is closed this term. After that, you will paint a picture of your own, and in the last week we’ll have a small exhibition in the hall. Your family and friends are welcome. Finally, some information about money. The course costs ninety pounds, which includes materials. I know that the sign in the hall says seventy, but that was the old price, and the price for the older course was a hundred and twenty, so we are somewhere in the middle. You can pay today or next week, by cash or card. Now, any questions before we start?

gaps.prompt: The workshop will go on for ___ weeks
gaps.explanation: It was advertised as six weeks but it is now eight weeks.
Thursday is for the pottery group, so the painting class is on Wednesday.

gaps.prompt: The classroom is located on the ___ floor
gaps.explanation: The music rooms are on the first floor; the art room is on the second.

gaps.prompt: Students are asked to bring an old ___ to protect their clothes
gaps.explanation: Brushes and paper are provided; they need an old shirt, and an apron is not enough.

gaps.prompt: A walk to the ___ takes place in the fourth week
gaps.explanation: The gallery in the old programme is closed, so they go to the museum on King Street.

gaps.prompt: Fees for the course come to ___ pounds
gaps.explanation: The sign says seventy and the older course cost a hundred and twenty, but the price now is ninety pounds.

parts.title: An interview with a street painter
parts.instructions: Listen to the interview and choose the correct answer.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Annabel, you draw enormous pictures on the pavement with chalk. How did you start?

turns.speaker: annabel
turns.text: By accident, really. A friend didn’t ask me, and I didn’t enter any competition, that came much later. One day I was waiting for a bus with a piece of chalk in my bag, I was bored, and I started to draw a flower on the ground. A man stopped, then another, and soon there was a small crowd. I just carried on.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: How long does a picture last?

turns.speaker: annabel
turns.text: It depends on the weather. A week is possible in dry weather, if people are careful, and I’d love it to last for months, but chalk isn’t paint. Usually a day or two, then the rain or the feet of people wash it away. In winter, even less.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: That sounds sad. How do you feel about your work disappearing?

turns.speaker: annabel
turns.text: People always ask that. I’m not upset at all, to be honest. I used to be, but not now. I like that it’s temporary, because it makes people stop and look today. A picture in a museum is always there, so you can look tomorrow. And rain doesn’t stop me: I paint in light rain when I can, with a big umbrella.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: Your three-dimensional pictures are famous. What do children enjoy most about them?

turns.speaker: annabel
turns.text: They love them! Some pictures look like a big hole in the ground, and children run to see. They don’t walk on them, because I ask them not to. I give them chalk of their own, and they colour next to me, which is nice, but the thing they really want is a photo. They stand at the edge of the hole, and the picture looks real. Parents take hundreds of photos.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What is the hardest thing about your job?

turns.speaker: annabel
turns.text: It’s not finding chalk, I can get it cheaply from a supplier. And people do look at my pictures, sometimes too much, so that’s not a worry either. It’s my body. I’m on my hands and knees for hours, and my knees hurt. In winter, it’s freezing, and my fingers go numb.

turns.speaker: host
turns.text: What would you say to someone who would like to try?

turns.speaker: annabel
turns.text: Start small, with just a flower or a face, and don’t worry about mistakes, because you can wipe them away. Don’t buy the most expensive chalk, the cheap one is fine at the beginning. And please don’t copy a famous painting exactly. Find your own idea, that’s much more fun.

questions.prompt: How long does a picture usually last?
questions.explanation: A week is possible in dry weather and she would love months, but usually a picture stays a day or two.
